doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Uncertainty about future touring and lost bookings
summary: Promoters are asking about autumn tours, but she will only travel when circumstances are right; Monk asks about gigs with Rossano and Eddie that were lost.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: November now. I just talked to a European promoter this morning and they said, “Oh we might have you over for two weeks in September.” I said, “Well it has to be worth the airfare and I have to know it’s — I can get there and come home, back here, you know what I mean? So there’s a lot more questions raised now about touring. I mean I used to get on a plane every other week like it was nothing you know. Now I have to think about my family. Now I have to think about travel routing and are there going to be flights back you know what I mean? And is the cost worth it if we’re going to have less people in the hall and do more concerts you know, like some of the concerts we’re going to have to do two concerts instead of one to get paid the same. So there’s a lot of complications yet. So I’ve just basically thought, well September is three months away. And of course I want to play. I love being on the road. I always have you know. I enjoy being with musicians, I enjoy being on stage, I enjoy playing. But it has to feel right. And after that experience in March I don’t want to rush out unless the circumstances are good.
Do you feel responsible for the other musicians that you may be taking with you? Maybe I didn’t ask that right, but is it a consideration about what they want to do also?

Yeah. I mean it’s very weird because when you commit to a gig and sign a contract, you know, you never want to cancel. It never feels right. I think a lot of the work in the fall, they’re all European musicians. You know one’s from France and the other two are in Germany. It’s just a matter — well even that, that’s a border to cross from France to Germany. I don’t know if the musician there would be able to make it, and I have basically said to them, “If I can’t make it, just find a sub for me.” “Yes, but you sing and you play.” “I know, well make the bass player sing.” I don’t know. I can’t help you on that end but the priority has to be safety first, family, and not to rush into anything. I mean there’s so many unknowns about this virus still. Second waves, third waves.
Do you have booked gigs with Rossano and Eddie?

Yeah we lost some. Yup. We had some in May, nice concerts, a couple of nice concerts we were supposed to do in May in Florida. A couple of jazz parties and hopefully December in Bern, Switzerland. We’ll see if Marians in Bern is opened up. That’s a beautiful club. I hope that happens.
